deities: Lord Ganesha (Swayambhu idol, Paschim Dwarpalak / Western Sentinel God)

history.summary: The Swayambhu (self-manifested) Ganapati temple at Ganpatipule is about 400 years old and one of the Ashta Dwar Devatas (eight welcoming deities), revered as Paschim Dwarpalak, the western sentinel of India. Folklore says Ganapati, offended by a remark of a native woman, moved from his original abode at Gule (Ganeshgule) to Pule, giving the place its name; the idol sprang from the soil and faces west, unlike most east-facing deities. A cowherd found the idol after a cow's milk flowed onto the spot; the brahmin renter Balbhatji Bhide built the first shrine here following a vision of the god. Maratha-era patrons included Nanasaheb Peshwa (Nandadeep lamp), Ramabai Peshwa (stone construction for pilgrims) and Madhavrao Peshwa (sabhamandap). The temple stands at the base of a hill around which pilgrims perform pradakshina.

name: Shree Ganpatipule Mandir (Swayambhu Ganapati Temple)
town_description: Ganpatipule is a small coastal town in Ratnagiri district on the Konkan coast of Maharashtra, about 375 km south of Mumbai, with a population of just over 1,200. It is a popular Hindu pilgrimage and beach destination, pairing the Swayambhu Ganapati temple with a clean white-sand beach, mangroves and coconut palms, plus MTDC water sports from November to May. The town is governed by the Ganpatipule Grampanchayat and lies near Ratnagiri city to the south and Chiplun to the north.
